policies.title: Unlisted ordinary national passports: Singapore visitor visa exemption
policies.summary: For the listed ordinary national passports, whose issuing country or region is absent from ICA's current visa-required countries-and-places list, MFA's current operational complement guidance says no Singapore visa is required.
conditions: This is limited to ordinary national passports represented by the listed ISO passport codes. It does not cover a refugee travel document, alien's passport, temporary UAE passport, Palestinian Authority passport, PRC Travel Document, HKSAR Document of Identity, Macao SAR Travel Permit, certificate of identity, laissez-passer, or another non-regular document.

It does not alter the separately evidenced treatment of PRC ordinary passports, Hong Kong SAR passports, Macao SAR passports, Taiwan ROC passports, or diplomatic, official, service, public-affairs and special passports.

The legal mechanism is a passport from a country approved by the Minister under Immigration Act section 9B(2). The statute does not publish a complete approved-country list; this normalized complement therefore rests on current ICA's visa-required list plus MFA's explicit operational complement statement, not on silence alone.

No pre-travel ETA is established by these sources. SGAC is a separate, free arrival and health declaration, not a visa or ETA; submit it within three days before arrival unless ICA's published exception applies.
This policy is for a short-term visitor seeking immigration clearance, not a Visa-Free Transit Facility. VFTF is a distinct, conditional less-than-96-hour route for eligible visa-required travellers.
A visa exemption does not guarantee admission. ICA determines entry and the duration of the electronic Visit Pass at the checkpoint; the Visit Pass is distinct from a visa.

Visitors must meet current general entry requirements, including an individually issued valid travel document, six months' passport validity for non-Singapore passport holders, and applicable onward-travel, funds, health and clearance requirements.

This policy does not authorize residence, employment, professional activity or paid work. ICA states that Short-Term Visit Pass holders may not engage in business, professional or paid employment activities.
